title: Acoustic Biomarkers for Alzheimer's Disease Detection from Spontaneous Speech
abstract: arXiv:2610.12500v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a major public health challenge, and early identification is crucial for timely intervention and care planning. Recent work has shown that speech-based digital biomarkers can capture subtle changes in vocal production, prosody, and timing that often precede or accompany cognitive decline. In this study, we investigate whether acoustic features extracted from spontaneous speech can reliably distinguish individuals with AD from healthy controls. Using a structured speech dataset derived from the Cookie Theft picture-description task, we extract clinically informative low-level descriptors spanning prosodic, spectral, and temporal domains, and evaluate a range of machine learning classifiers. Our results indicate that acoustic biomarkers carry strong discriminative value, with the best-performing models achieving clinically meaningful separation between diagnostic groups. translated_title: 基于自发言语的声学生物标志物用于阿尔茨海默病检测
translated_abstract: 阿尔茨海默病（AD）仍然是一个重大的公共卫生挑战，早期识别对于及时干预和护理规划至关重要。最近的研究表明，基于语音的数字生物标志物能够捕捉嗓音产生、韵律和时序方面的细微变化，这些变化往往先于或伴随认知衰退出现。在本研究中，我们探讨从自发言语中提取的声学特征是否能够可靠地区分阿尔茨海默病患者与健康对照者。我们使用源自“饼干失窃”图片描述任务的结构化语音数据集，提取了涵盖韵律、频谱和时域的具有临床价值的低级描述符，并评估了多种机器学习分类器。我们的结果表明，声学生物标志物具有很强的判别价值，表现最佳的模型在诊断组之间实现了具有临床意义的区分。这些发现支持了使用……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 本研究证明从“饼干失窃”图片描述等自发言语中提取的韵律、频谱和时域声学特征，结合机器学习分类器，可以有效区分阿尔茨海默病患者与健康人群，为AD的早期筛查提供了一种具有临床意义的语音生物标志物方法。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that acoustic biomarkers—prosodic, spectral, and temporal low-level descriptors extracted from spontaneous speech—combined with machine learning classifiers can reliably distinguish Alzheimer's disease patients from healthy controls, offering a clinically meaningful speech-based approach for early AD detection.
